card.name: Pinyin romanization of Chinese terms
card.fires_on: Inside or right after pinyin spellings of Chinese names and terms, especially in parenthetical glosses like 'pinyin: Xīn Wénhuà Yùndòng'. It fires on syllables and the colon after 'Pinyin'.

modes.label: Inside pinyin syllables
modes.description: Partway through romanized Chinese words with tone marks, in a gloss after the Chinese characters.
modes.example: Culture Movement (simplified Chinese: 新文化运动; traditional Chinese: 新文化運動; pinyin: Xīn Wénhuà Yù<<nd>>òng) of the mid 19

modes.label: Pinyin label and start
modes.description: The colon after 'Pinyin' or the first letter of the pinyin spelling that follows.
modes.example: -mātratā, vijñapti-mātra, citta-mātra; Chinese: 唯識; Pinyin<<:>> wei shi; Japanese: yuish

card.writes: It promotes Vietnamese-looking syllables such as ' chí', ' mé' and ' báo', so it pushes toward accented Latin-script syllables rather than Slavic or Chinese tokens.
card.plain: It lights up when text spells out Chinese words in Latin letters with accents, like pinyin.
